transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-09-04
Start: 09:24 UTC
Duration: ~58 mins
Recording: Fireflies auto
Attendees: Jordan Park (Redwood AE), Liam Chen (Redwood SE), Maya Patel (Redwood CSM), Anna Soto (Hearth Head of ML), Marcus Doyle (Hearth Platform Eng), Priya Kaur (Hearth Security)

Summary:
- Jordan opened with a 10-min console walkthrough focused on per-route usage analytics, token/cost breakdowns, and how Optimize surfaces batching/caching recommendations.
- Liam demoed a live per-route dashboard, drill-down to token-level cost, and a routing policy change that fell back to a cheaper model variant for low-priority routes.
- Security questions from Priya around KMS, audit logs, and SSO; Redwood to share SOC2 docs.
- Agreed next steps: pricing spreadsheet, pilot benchmark, security doc exchange.

Topics covered:
- Per-route dashboards and tags
- Token-level cost attribution and breakdown by model/route
- Optimize recommendations: batching / KV prefix caching / quantization suggestions
- Routing policies & canary rollouts
- Hosted vs Dedicated cost tradeoffs
- Security: KMS, SSO/SAML, audit logs, data residency

Transcript body:
[00:00] Jordan: ok hey everyone, thanks for joining, um quick housekeeping, I'm Jordan Park from Redwood, with Liam on the demo side and Maya on success.
[00:18] Anna: hi thanks, excited, we wanted to focus mostly on the console cost stuff and understanding per-route attribution for our multi-tenant inference platform.
[00:35] Jordan: perfect, that aligns well. I'll share my screen, and I'll jump right to the Console Insights page where you can see per-route cost by day, week, month. (screen share noise) apologies if the resolution is a bit off on the call.
[01:02] Liam: yeah and just to call out up front, two things we surface a lot: token-level cost attribution and per-route latency percentiles, so you can see expensive routes not just by volume but by cost per token.
[01:22] Marcus: when you say token-level, are you breaking out request vs completion tokens? we need to map that back to our billing buckets.
[01:33] Liam: yes, the breakdown is request_tokens / response_tokens and we also show model multiplier — if you pick a larger model the per-token cost is scaled, you can filter by model name. sometimes the model names get transcribed funny in the export but the ids are accurate.
[01:52] Anna: is that traceable to a customer id or tenancy? we run dozens of teams, need attribution per internal team.
[02:02] Jordan: absolutely, you can tag routes with tenant IDs or team slugs, and the dashboard will aggregate by tag. i'll show an example — in Heart... Hearth you could tag route: "billing-inference" and it will roll up.
[02:20] (static)
[02:28] Liam: jumping to a per-route page now — here you see a traffic heatmap, cost per hour, and a cost breakdown by token type and by model variant. the cool trick is the cost waterfall: model compute, queueing overhead, egress.
[02:52] Marcus: queueing overhead? can you quickly explain where that comes from?
[03:00] Liam: sure, that is primarily the latency cost that comes from batching windows and GPU time slices — it's approximate but helps identify routes that incur lots of tiny batches, which can be expensive.
[03:17] Anna: do you have suggestions to reduce that? we have a lot of low-latency requests that are single-sentence.
[03:27] Liam: Optimize will suggest batching thresholds, and also prefix/KV cache rules for routes where prompts share common prefixes. it surfaced a rule in our sample data that would've saved ~22% on per-token cost by caching common instructions.
[03:44] Anna: is that automatic? or does it require dev changes?
[03:49] Liam: it's a mix — we can wire automatic caching for certain route patterns, but typically customers add a small SDK call to consult the cache layer. we can show a code snippet. 
[04:02] Jordan: and on the cost side, you can set route-specific routing policies: e.g., route A uses fast-llm-x-16 with a higher cost SLA, route B falls back to medium-llm-x-8 for non-critical queries. watch the demo for the fallback.
[04:24] [05:10] Liam: ok changing the routing rule now — I'm switching this 'summary' route to a policy that prefers the cheaper variant in off-peak hours, and you can see the cost projection update in the top-right bar, it's recalculating estimates based on your sample traffic distribution.
[05:36] Priya: on that note, what about privacy? our security team wants to ensure keys & logs are protected — KMS integration and audit logs are must-haves.
[05:49] Jordan: yep so we support customer-managed keys (KMS/HSM) for Private and Dedicated, and we store audit trails in an append-only log with export options. i'll share SOC2 and the audit log doc after the call.
[06:07] Priya: do you encrypt in transit and at rest? and can logs be forwarded to our SIEM?
[06:14] Liam: TLS in transit, AES-256 at rest, and log forwarding to Splunk/Datadog is supported via syslog/HTTP collectors.
[06:26] Anna: quick nit, are the per-route dashboards retroactive? if we tag routes today, can you backfill prior traffic?
[06:34] Liam: yes, if the historical raw token events are available we can re-aggregate, but for hosted tiers there is a retention window. Dedicated/Private gives you longer retention for backfills.
[06:46] (mumble)
[07:00] Jordan: on pricing, i'll be sending a customized worksheet but the one thing to watch is unit economics: batching/caching/quantization recommendations can move you from $0.00x/token to a lower number — quantization usually has quality tradeoffs we can simulate.
[07:19] Marcus: simulation — how do you measure quality impact?
[07:25] Liam: we run a small eval harness tied to your prompt set, produce A/B outputs with the quantized model and compare heuristics like exact-match, BLEU-ish scores, and human review when needed. Optimize stores the eval history and alerts on regressions.
[07:45] Anna: do you support canary rollouts? we want to slowly move teams to newer quantized models.
[07:51] Jordan: yes, Console supports canary percentages per-route with auto-fallback if latency or quality dips beyond thresholds.
[08:03] Anna: show me the route insights for, say, our 'customer_chat' route.
[08:10] Liam: sure, switching. (click) here's customer_chat — high qps in US-East, median latency 120ms, p95 340ms, monthly token count 1.2M, cost $3,400 last month. you can click into day-by-day, see spikes and the originating tenant tags.
[08:33] Marcus: hmm that p95 is surprising, maybe some tail latencies from cold KV cache?
[08:40] Liam: possible, and the timeline shows correlation spikes when batch size drops. you can enable warmers / keepalives in the route config to reduce cold-starts.
[08:52] Anna: we'd like to run a dedicated pool for chat-heavy routes, but worries about committed spend. what's the guardrail?
[09:01] Jordan: Dedicated gives predictable throughput and lower per-token cost at scale — we typically model 3-6 month commit windows; we can propose a hybrid: burst into hosted for spikes while primary traffic goes to Dedicated. the console shows projected monthly spends for both modes side-by-side.
[09:20] Marcus: are there SLA numbers for Dedicated?
[09:25] Jordan: yes, Dedicated includes a 99.9% uptime SLA and latency SLOs depending on the instance class, we'll include those in the contract.
[09:33] Priya: one last security question — SAML/SSO for the Console? RBAC?
[09:39] Liam: SAML SSO, SCIM provisioning, and fine-grained RBAC are supported. for Private installs you can tie into your IdP directly.
[09:48] Anna: can you show the cost explorer export? we want to push this into our finance dashboard.
[09:53] Liam: export is CSV/Parquet and you can include route tags, model ids, token counts, cost line items. (typing) here's an example link I just dropped in chat: https://redwood.example.com/shared/hearth-cost-sample.csv — note: demo link only.
[10:12] Jordan: quick pause for questions.
[10:17] Anna: in terms of openness, do you allow custom models? we have some internal fine-tuned models.
[10:23] Jordan: yes, Dedicated and Private support customer models; hosted supports bring-your-own in certain regions, there are compatibility checks for the serving runtime.
[10:34] Marcus: about Optimize — does it create live rules or just recommendations?
[10:39] Liam: Optimize surfaces both recommendations and a 'apply' toggle. customers can auto-apply low-risk rules (cache TTLs, batching thresholds) and we provide an audit trail of changes.
[10:50] Anna: what's the rollback mechanism if a rule causes regressions?
[10:55] Liam: auto-rollback based on quality/latency SLO breaches; rollouts are incremental and you can set thresholds.
[11:06] Jordan: ok running a short example of cost impact — I have two scenarios for Hearth: hosted-only and hybrid dedicated + hosted bursting. watch the projected cost delta as I change QPS and batch size. (screen share)
[11:34] Marcus: the hybrid looks attractive but we'd need a 90-day forecast, can you produce that?
[11:40] Jordan: yes I'll add that to the cost spreadsheet.
[11:45] Priya: any compliance certifications beyond SOC2? we may need ISO 27001.
[11:52] Jordan: we have SOC2 Type II; ISO is on the roadmap and we can share the controls map that shows alignment to ISO clauses.
[12:03] Anna: got it. switching topic briefly, our infra team is picky about network egress — can you pin workloads to specific regions for data residency?
[12:11] Liam: yes region pinning and routing policies exist; you can enforce region-only routing and disallow cross-region fallbacks.
[12:21] (brief pause)
[12:30] Jordan: thought: for the pilot, Liam will run a small cluster with representative prompts and share per-route screenshots so you can validate the cost/p95 improvements.
[12:42] Marcus: that would be good. also can you include a trace example for a slow request? we use Jaeger and would like to see how Redwood traces correlate.
[12:51] Liam: we support OpenTelemetry traces and can export to Jaeger, we'll include a sample trace in the benchmark artifacts.
[13:02] Anna: one more product detail — in the console, can we create synthetic workloads to simulate peak QPS for budgeting?
[13:10] Liam: there's a load generator tool for Dedicated customers, and for hosted we can run controlled test bursts via the test harness.
[13:20] Jordan: ok wrapping up, recap of actions: send pricing, schedule pilot, share SOC2 and KMS notes. anything else?
[13:32] Priya: please include a short note on key rotation/expiry policies and how long logs are retained by default.
[13:39] Jordan: will do.
[13:44] Anna: thanks, this was useful.
[13:47] Jordan: thanks everyone, we'll follow up in email with attachments.

(End of recorded segment; Fireflies trimmed last few minutes)
